stem: Look at the power 6<sup>4</sup>. Which statement is true?

choices.t: The base is 6. The exponent 4 means 6 is used as a factor 4 times: 6 × 6 × 6 × 6.
choices.why: Yes. The base is the factor, and the exponent counts how many times it is used.

choices.t: The base is 4. The exponent 6 means 4 is used as a factor 6 times: 4 × 4 × 4 × 4 × 4 × 4.
choices.why: You mixed up the two numbers. The big number is the base; the small raised number is the exponent.

choices.t: The base is 6. The exponent 4 means 6 is multiplied by 4 one time: 6 × 4.
choices.why: An exponent is not a regular factor. It tells how many times the base is used as a factor.

choices.t: The base is 6. The exponent 4 means 6 is added 4 times: 6 + 6 + 6 + 6.
choices.why: An exponent means repeated multiplication, not repeated addition.

hint: The small raised number tells you how many times to use the big number.
explain: The base is the big number on the line: 6.
The exponent is the small raised number: 4.

stem:
Simplify. Write your answer as a single power.
(m2)4 · m3

choices.why: Yes. (m<sup>2</sup>)<sup>4</sup> = m<sup>8</sup>, then m<sup>8</sup> · m<sup>3</sup> = m<sup>11</sup>.
You added all three exponents. A power of a power multiplies: 2 × 4 = 8 first.
You multiplied all three exponents. When you multiply m<sup>8</sup> · m<sup>3</sup>, add the exponents.
You used the rules backward. Power of a power multiplies (2 × 4); same base times same base adds.

hint: Do the power of a power first, then multiply powers with the same base.
explain: Power of a power: multiply the exponents. (m<sup>2</sup>)<sup>4</sup> = m<sup>2 × 4</sup> = m<sup>8</sup>.
Product of powers: add the exponents. m<sup>8</sup> · m<sup>3</sup> = m<sup>8 + 3</sup>.

stem: What is the value of 5<sup>0</sup> · 4<sup>−2</sup>?

choices.why: Yes. 5<sup>0</sup> = 1 and 4<sup>−2</sup> = {{1|16}}, so the product is {{1|16}}.
A zero exponent does not give 0. Any nonzero number to the zero power is 1.
5<sup>0</sup> is not 5. Any nonzero number to the zero power is 1.
A negative exponent does not make the number negative. It means take the reciprocal: 4<sup>−2</sup> = {{1|4<sup>2</sup>}}.

hint: What does a zero exponent always give? What does a negative exponent tell you to flip?
explain: 5<sup>0</sup> = 1 (any nonzero number to the zero power is 1).

stem:
Simplify.
{{18x7y4|6x2y}}

choices.why: You subtracted the coefficients (18 − 6). Divide them: 18 ÷ 6 = 3.
You added the exponents. When you divide powers with the same base, subtract them.
The y on the bottom has an exponent of 1. Subtract it: 4 − 1 = 3.

hint: Divide the numbers, then subtract the exponents for each letter.

stem:
Simplify completely.
{{(3a3b)2 · 2ab4|6a5b2}}

choices.why: Yes. The top is 18a<sup>7</sup>b<sup>6</sup>, and 18a<sup>7</sup>b<sup>6</sup> ÷ 6a<sup>5</sup>b<sup>2</sup> = 3a<sup>2</sup>b<sup>4</sup>.
You did not square the 3. In (3a<sup>3</sup>b)<sup>2</sup>, every factor is squared, so 3<sup>2</sup> = 9.
You doubled the 3 instead of squaring it. 3<sup>2</sup> = 3 × 3 = 9, not 3 × 2.
You added exponents inside the power. A power of a power multiplies: (a<sup>3</sup>)<sup>2</sup> = a<sup>6</sup>.

hint: Square every factor inside the parentheses first, then multiply, then divide.

stem:
Simplify. Write your answer using only positive exponents.
{{(4x−3y5)(3x7y−2)|6x0y6}}

choices.why: Yes. The top is 12x<sup>4</sup>y<sup>3</sup>, the bottom is 6y<sup>6</sup>, and y<sup>3 − 6</sup> = y<sup>−3</sup> moves to the bottom.
The y exponent is 3 − 6 = −3, not 3. A negative exponent means the y belongs in the denominator.
You treated x<sup>−3</sup> as x<sup>3</sup>. Add with the sign: −3 + 7 = 4.
x<sup>0</sup> is 1, not x. So there is no x left on the bottom.

hint: Remember that x to the zero power is 1, and keep track of the signs when you add exponents.
explain: Top: 4 × 3 = 12, x<sup>−3 + 7</sup> = x<sup>4</sup>, y<sup>5 + (−2)</sup> = y<sup>3</sup>. So 12x<sup>4</sup>y<sup>3</sup>.

stem: Devon simplified (5<sup>3</sup>)<sup>4</sup> · 5<sup>2</sup> ÷ 5<sup>−5</sup>. His work is in the table. Which statement is correct?

choices.t: Steps 1 and 3 are wrong. The correct answer is 5<sup>19</sup>.
choices.why: Yes. (5<sup>3</sup>)<sup>4</sup> = 5<sup>12</sup>, then 5<sup>14</sup>, then 14 − (−5) = 19.

choices.t: Only Step 1 is wrong. The correct answer is 5<sup>9</sup>.
choices.why: Step 1 is wrong, but so is Step 3. Subtracting −5 is the same as adding 5: 14 − (−5) = 19.

choices.t: Only Step 3 is wrong. The correct answer is 5<sup>14</sup>.
choices.why: Step 3 is wrong, but so is Step 1. A power of a power multiplies: 3 × 4 = 12, not 3 + 4.

choices.t: All three steps are right. The answer is 5<sup>4</sup>.
choices.why: Check each rule again. Steps 1 and 3 each use a rule the wrong way.

hint: Check each step: power of a power multiplies, and dividing subtracts (watch the negative sign).
explain: Steps 1 and 3 were wrong. The answer is 5<sup>19</sup>.

stem: Look at the pattern in the table. Which explanation correctly shows what 5<sup>0</sup> and 5<sup>−1</sup> equal?

choices.t: Each time the exponent goes down 1, you divide by 5. So 5<sup>0</sup> = 5 ÷ 5 = 1 and 5<sup>−1</sup> = 1 ÷ 5 = {{1|5}}.
choices.why: Yes. Going down the table divides by 5 each time, so the pattern gives 1 and then the reciprocal of 5.

choices.t: Each time the exponent goes down 1, you subtract 5. So 5<sup>0</sup> = 5 − 5 = 0 and 5<sup>−1</sup> = 0 − 5 = −5.
choices.why: The pattern is not subtraction: 25 to 5 is not “minus 5.” Each step divides by 5.

choices.t: Each time the exponent goes down 1, you divide by 5. So 5<sup>0</sup> = 1, and 5<sup>−1</sup> = −5 because the exponent is negative.
choices.why: The first part is right, but a negative exponent does not make the number negative. 1 ÷ 5 = {{1|5}}.

choices.t: Using no exponent leaves the 5 unchanged, so 5<sup>0</sup> = 5. Then 5<sup>−1</sup> = 5 ÷ 5 = 1.
choices.why: An exponent of 0 is not the same as no exponent (which means an exponent of 1). The pattern gives 5 ÷ 5 = 1 for the zero power.

hint: How do you get from 125 to 25 to 5? Keep doing the same thing.
explain: Going down the table: 125 ÷ 5 = 25, and 25 ÷ 5 = 5. Each step divides by 5.
This works for any base a except 0, because you can never divide by 0.

stem: Write (2<sup>5</sup> · 4<sup>2</sup>)<sup>3</sup> ÷ 8<sup>4</sup> as a single power of 2. Which answer has correct reasoning?

choices.why: Yes. Rewrite every base as a power of 2, then use the power, product, and quotient rules.

choices.t: 2<sup>17</sup>, because you can read 4<sup>2</sup> as 2<sup>2</sup> and 8<sup>4</sup> as 2<sup>4</sup>, so (2<sup>7</sup>)<sup>3</sup> ÷ 2<sup>4</sup> = 2<sup>21 − 4</sup>.
choices.why: You cannot just change the base. 4 = 2<sup>2</sup>, so 4<sup>2</sup> = (2<sup>2</sup>)<sup>2</sup> = 2<sup>4</sup>.
You added exponents for a power of a power. (2<sup>3</sup>)<sup>4</sup> = 2<sup>12</sup> and (2<sup>9</sup>)<sup>3</sup> = 2<sup>27</sup>; multiply them.
The power of 3 applies to everything inside the parentheses, so 2<sup>4</sup> must be cubed too.

hint: Start by writing 4 and 8 as powers of 2.

stem: Write 0.00038 in scientific notation.

choices.why: Yes. Move the decimal 4 places right to get 3.8. The number is less than 1, so the exponent is negative.
A positive exponent makes a big number. 0.00038 is less than 1, so the exponent must be negative.
You counted only the three zeros. Count the hops to land right after the 3: that is 4 hops.
You counted all 5 decimal places. Stop after the first nonzero digit (the 3): that is 4 hops.

hint: Move the decimal so exactly one nonzero digit is in front of it. Count the hops.
explain: The coefficient must be at least 1 and less than 10: 3.8.
The number is less than 1, so the exponent is negative.

stem: Write 6.05 × 10<sup>5</sup> in standard form.

choices.why: Yes. Move the decimal 5 places to the right: 6.05 → 605,000.
You wrote 5 zeros after 605. The digits 0 and 5 already use 2 of the 5 places, so add only 3 zeros.
You moved the decimal only 4 places. The exponent 5 means 5 places.
You moved the decimal left. A positive exponent means a big number, so move it right.

hint: A positive exponent means the number is big. Which way should the decimal move?
explain: The exponent is a positive 5, so move the decimal 5 places to the right.

stem: A video website had 3,912,450,000 visits in one month. Which is the best estimate written as a single digit times a power of 10?

choices.why: You counted all 10 digits. Count the hops from the end to the spot after the 3: that is 9.
You chopped off the decimals. 3.91 is closer to 4 than to 3, so round up.
A negative exponent makes a tiny number. This is a huge number, so the exponent is positive.

hint: Put the decimal right after the first digit, count the hops, then round to one digit.
explain: Move the decimal to sit after the 3: 3.91245.
That took 9 hops to the left, so the power is 10<sup>9</sup>.

stem: A city has about 8 × 10<sup>6</sup> people. A small town has about 2 × 10<sup>4</sup> people. How many times as many people live in the city?

choices.why: You divided only the coefficients. Also divide the powers of 10: 10<sup>6</sup> ÷ 10<sup>4</sup> = 10<sup>2</sup>.
You subtracted 8 − 2. To find “how many times as many,” divide: 8 ÷ 2 = 4.
You kept the town's exponent. When you divide, subtract the exponents: 6 − 4 = 2.

hint: “How many times as many” means divide the bigger number by the smaller one.
explain: 4 × 10<sup>2</sup> = 400, so the city has 400 times as many people.

stem: The table shows the widths of five tiny things. Which list is in order from smallest to largest?

choices.t: Bacterium, blood cell, pollen, hair, dust mite
choices.why: Yes. 10<sup>−6</sup> is smallest, then 10<sup>−5</sup>, then 10<sup>−4</sup>. Inside each group, compare the coefficients.

choices.t: Bacterium, pollen, dust mite, blood cell, hair
choices.why: You compared only the coefficients. Look at the exponents first; they matter much more.

choices.t: Dust mite, pollen, hair, bacterium, blood cell
choices.why: You treated 10<sup>−4</sup> as the smallest. −6 is less than −4, so 10<sup>−6</sup> is the smallest power.

choices.t: Dust mite, hair, pollen, blood cell, bacterium
choices.why: This list goes from largest to smallest. The question asks for smallest first.

hint: Compare the exponents first. Which negative exponent is the smallest number?
explain: 10<sup>−6</sup> group: 2 < 8, so bacterium, then blood cell.

stem: A hit song has 2,987,000,000 streams. A new song has 4,890,000 streams. Round each to a single digit times a power of 10. About how many times as many streams does the hit song have?

choices.why: You changed 0.6 to 6 but did not fix the exponent. 0.6 × 10<sup>3</sup> = 6 × 10<sup>2</sup> = 600.
You counted all 7 digits of 4,890,000. It is 4.89 × 10<sup>6</sup>, so round to 5 × 10<sup>6</sup>.
You chopped 4.89 down to 4. Round instead: 4.89 rounds up to 5.

hint: Round each number first, then divide the coefficients and subtract the exponents.
explain: Divide the coefficients: 3 ÷ 5 = 0.6. Subtract the exponents: 9 − 6 = 3.
The hit song has about 600 times as many streams.

stem: Four students wrote a number in scientific notation. Only one student is correct. Who is it?

choices.why: Yes. 5.2 is between 1 and 10, and 0.00052 is less than 1, so the exponent is negative 4.
0.00071 is less than 1, so the exponent must be negative. It should be 7.1 × 10<sup>−4</sup>.
38.6 is not less than 10. Move the decimal one more place left and add 1: 3.86 × 10<sup>5</sup>.
The exponent is off by one. 52,000 is 5.2 with 4 hops, so it is 5.2 × 10<sup>4</sup>.

hint: Check two things: Is the coefficient from 1 up to 10? Does the exponent's sign and size match the number?
explain: Jada: the number is less than 1, so the exponent should be negative.
Marcus: 38.6 is too big for a coefficient; fix it to 3.86 × 10<sup>5</sup>.

stem:
The Moon is about 384,000,000 m from Earth. Which answer rewrites this distance in a good unit for reporting it and gives a correct reason?
1 km = 1,000 m   1 m = 1,000 mm

choices.t: 3.84 × 10<sup>5</sup> km, because kilometers are used for long distances and 384,000 is easy to picture.
choices.why: Yes. 3.84 × 10<sup>8</sup> ÷ 10<sup>3</sup> = 3.84 × 10<sup>5</sup> km, a sensible unit for space distances.

choices.t: 3.84 × 10<sup>11</sup> km, because kilometers are bigger, so you multiply by 1,000 to change units.
choices.why: Kilometers are bigger, so you need fewer of them. Divide by 1,000, not multiply.

choices.t: 3.84 × 10<sup>11</sup> mm, because a smaller unit always makes a measurement more exact.
choices.why: The math is right, but millimeters are far too small for this. The number gets even harder to picture.

choices.t: 3.84 × 10<sup>8</sup> km, because the number does not change when you change units.
choices.why: When the unit changes, the number must change too. 1 km is 1,000 m, so divide by 1,000.

hint: Pick a unit close to the size of the distance. Is a kilometer bigger or smaller than a meter?
explain: 1 km = 1,000 m = 10<sup>3</sup> m, so divide by 10<sup>3</sup>: 3.84 × 10<sup>8</sup> ÷ 10<sup>3</sup> = 3.84 × 10<sup>5</sup> km.
That is 384,000 km, a number that is easy to read and compare.
Kilometers fit very long distances, so km is a good unit here.

stem: An ant has a mass of about 3 × 10<sup>−6</sup> kg. An elephant has a mass of about 6 × 10<sup>3</sup> kg. Kai says, “The exponents are 9 apart, so the elephant is about 10<sup>9</sup> times as heavy.” Which statement is correct?

choices.t: Kai is right about the size. 3 − (−6) = 9, and the exact answer is 2 × 10<sup>9</sup> times.
choices.why: Yes. The exponents give the order of magnitude, and 6 ÷ 3 = 2 gives the exact multiple.

choices.t: Kai is wrong. The exponents are 6 − 3 = 3 apart, so it is 2 × 10<sup>3</sup> times.
choices.why: You ignored the negative sign. From −6 up to 3 is 9 steps, not 3.

choices.t: Kai is right, and the exact answer is 10<sup>9</sup> times, since the coefficients do not matter.
choices.why: The exponents give a good estimate, but the coefficients still count: 6 ÷ 3 = 2.

choices.t: Kai is right about the size, and the exact answer is 3 × 10<sup>9</sup> times.
choices.why: You subtracted the coefficients (6 − 3). To compare by “times,” divide: 6 ÷ 3 = 2.

hint: Each step up in the exponent means 10 times as big. Count the steps from −6 to 3.
explain: The exponent shows the order of magnitude. Each 1 up means 10 times as large.
From −6 up to 3 is 3 − (−6) = 9 steps, so about 10<sup>9</sup> times. Kai's estimate makes sense.
The elephant is about 2 billion times as heavy as the ant.

stem:
Multiply. Write the answer in scientific notation.
(2 × 10−4)(3.5 × 109)

choices.why: You dropped the negative sign. −4 + 9 = 5, not 13.
You added the coefficients. Multiply them: 2 × 3.5 = 7.
You multiplied the exponents. When you multiply powers of 10, add the exponents.

hint: Multiply the coefficients. Add the exponents (watch the sign).
explain: 7 is between 1 and 10, so the answer is 7 × 10<sup>5</sup>.

stem:
Divide. Write the answer in scientific notation.
{{8.4 × 10−3|4 × 105}}

choices.why: You added the exponents. When you divide, subtract: −3 − 5 = −8.
You subtracted in the wrong order. Top minus bottom: −3 − 5 = −8.
You subtracted the coefficients. Divide them: 8.4 ÷ 4 = 2.1.

hint: Divide the coefficients. Subtract the exponents: top minus bottom.
explain: 2.1 is between 1 and 10, so the answer is 2.1 × 10<sup>−8</sup>.

stem: Ty multiplied (6 × 10<sup>4</sup>)(9 × 10<sup>3</sup>) and got 54 × 10<sup>7</sup>. The coefficient 54 is too big. Which is the same number written correctly in scientific notation?

choices.why: Yes. 54 = 5.4 × 10, so move the decimal left one place and add 1 to the exponent.
You subtracted 1. Making the coefficient smaller means the exponent must go up to keep the same value.
You moved the decimal but kept the exponent. That makes the number 10 times too small.
You added 1 to the exponent but did not move the decimal. That makes the number 10 times too big.

hint: 54 = 5.4 × 10. Where does that extra 10 go?
explain: 54 is not less than 10, so rewrite it: 54 = 5.4 × 10<sup>1</sup>.

stem: One grain of rice has a mass of about 2.5 × 10<sup>−2</sup> grams. A bag holds about 4 × 10<sup>4</sup> grains. What is the total mass of the rice?

choices.why: You changed 10 to 1 but forgot to add 1 to the exponent. 10 × 10<sup>2</sup> = 1 × 10<sup>3</sup>.
You multiplied the exponents (−2 × 4). When you multiply powers of 10, add them.
You divided. Many grains that each have the same mass means multiply.

hint: Each grain has the same mass, and there are many grains. Should you multiply or divide?
explain: 10 is too big for a coefficient: 10 × 10<sup>2</sup> = 1 × 10<sup>3</sup>.

stem: A factory makes 2,400,000 bolts each year. Each bolt has a mass of 3.5 × 10<sup>−2</sup> kg. What is the total mass of the bolts made in one year?

choices.why: You wrote 2,400,000 as 2.4 × 10<sup>7</sup> by counting all 7 digits. It takes 6 hops, so it is 10<sup>6</sup>.
You dropped the negative sign. 6 + (−2) = 4, not 8.
You added the coefficients. Multiply them: 2.4 × 3.5 = 8.4.

hint: First write 2,400,000 in scientific notation. Then multiply.

stem: A water plant sends out 1.2 × 10<sup>8</sup> liters of water each day. It is shared equally by 1.5 × 10<sup>5</sup> homes. How many liters does each home get in a 30-day month?

choices.why: Yes. Each home gets 8 × 10<sup>2</sup> L per day, and 8 × 10<sup>2</sup> × 30 = 2.4 × 10<sup>4</sup> L.
That is the amount for one day. Multiply by 30 to get a whole month.
You rewrote 0.8 × 10<sup>3</sup> as 8 × 10<sup>3</sup>. Moving the decimal right means subtract 1: 8 × 10<sup>2</sup>.
You multiplied by 3 instead of 30. 30 = 3 × 10<sup>1</sup>, so add 1 more to the exponent.

hint: First find the liters per home for one day. Then think about 30 days.
explain: Fix the coefficient: 0.8 × 10<sup>3</sup> = 8 × 10<sup>2</sup> L per day (800 L).

stem: Each hair on a person's head grows about 3.5 × 10<sup>−4</sup> m per day. A person has about 1 × 10<sup>5</sup> hairs. How many days would it take for the combined growth of all the hairs to reach 7 × 10<sup>3</sup> m? Which answer has correct steps?

choices.t: 2 × 10<sup>2</sup> days: all hairs grow (3.5 × 10<sup>−4</sup>)(1 × 10<sup>5</sup>) = 3.5 × 10<sup>1</sup> m a day, and (7 × 10<sup>3</sup>) ÷ (3.5 × 10<sup>1</sup>) = 2 × 10<sup>2</sup>.
choices.why: Yes. Multiply to get the growth of all hairs per day, then divide the total by that daily amount.

choices.t: 2 × 10<sup>7</sup> days: divide the total by the growth of each hair, (7 × 10<sup>3</sup>) ÷ (3.5 × 10<sup>−4</sup>) = 2 × 10<sup>7</sup>.
choices.why: That uses the growth of just one hair. First multiply by the number of hairs to get the daily growth of all of them.

choices.t: 2.45 × 10<sup>5</sup> days: all hairs grow 3.5 × 10<sup>1</sup> m a day, and (7 × 10<sup>3</sup>) × (3.5 × 10<sup>1</sup>) = 2.45 × 10<sup>5</sup>.
choices.why: Multiplying gives m × m per day, which is not days. Divide the total by the amount per day.

choices.t: 5 × 10<sup>−3</sup> days: all hairs grow 3.5 × 10<sup>1</sup> m a day, and (3.5 × 10<sup>1</sup>) ÷ (7 × 10<sup>3</sup>) = 5 × 10<sup>−3</sup>.
choices.why: You divided in the wrong order. To see how many days fit, divide the total by the amount per day.

hint: Step 1: how much do all the hairs grow in one day? Step 2: how many of those days fit into the total?
explain: All hairs grow the same amount, so multiply: (3.5 × 10<sup>−4</sup>)(1 × 10<sup>5</sup>) = 3.5 × 10<sup>1</sup> m per day (35 m).
Days = total ÷ amount per day, because m ÷ (m per day) = days: (7 × 10<sup>3</sup>) ÷ (3.5 × 10<sup>1</sup>).

stem:
An Olympic pool holds about 2.5 × 103 m3 of water. Each cubic meter of water has a mass of 1 × 103 kg. Riley says the water's mass is 2.5 × 109 kg. Which response is correct?
1 metric ton = 1,000 kg

choices.t: Not reasonable. 2,500 × 1,000 = 2,500,000, so it is 2.5 × 10<sup>6</sup> kg, or 2,500 metric tons.
choices.why: Yes. Riley multiplied the exponents; adding them gives 10<sup>6</sup>, and 2,500 metric tons is easier to picture.

choices.t: Reasonable. Since 3 × 3 = 9, multiplying 10<sup>3</sup> by 10<sup>3</sup> gives 10<sup>9</sup>, so Riley is right.
choices.why: When you multiply powers of 10, add the exponents: 3 + 3 = 6, not 3 × 3.

choices.t: Not reasonable. Since 10<sup>3</sup> ÷ 10<sup>3</sup> = 10<sup>0</sup>, the mass is only 2.5 × 10<sup>0</sup> = 2.5 kg.
choices.why: Many cubic meters that each have the same mass means multiply, not divide. 2.5 kg is far too small.

choices.t: Not reasonable. The mass is 2.5 × 10<sup>6</sup> kg, which is 2.5 × 10<sup>9</sup> metric tons.
choices.why: The kilograms are right, but a ton is bigger than a kilogram, so there are fewer tons. Divide by 1,000.

hint: Estimate first: about how many kilograms is 2,500 cubic meters if each one is 1,000 kg?
explain: Estimate: 2,500 × 1,000 = 2,500,000 kg. Riley's 2,500,000,000 kg is 1,000 times too big.
Metric tons are a good unit because 2,500 is easier to picture than 2,500,000.
